# Cūḷabodhijātaka (Ja 443)

**ID:** Ja 443
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)
**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Cūḷabodhijātaka
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul9.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Cūḷabodhijātaka* (Ja 443, also spelled *Cullabodhijātaka*) belongs to the Dasanipāta of the Jātaka collection [Morris 1882]. According to the frame story, the Buddha recounted this birth tale while residing at Jetavana with reference to a passionate man. In the narrative, the Bodhisatta renounces worldly life as the virtuous ascetic Cūḷabodhi and dwells in the royal park at Benares alongside his former wife, a brāhmaṇī of golden complexion who has likewise undertaken ascetic renunciation [Bareau; Hazra 1994; Morris 1882]. When the local king forcibly abducts the ascetic's former wife, she steadfastly rejects the king's advances, while Cūḷabodhi refuses to succumb to anger in order to safeguard his moral discipline (*sīla*); upon being questioned by the astonished king, the Bodhisatta delivers verses praising the eradication of anger [Anandajoti 2010; Hazra 1994; War Yar Mein Da 2015].

 AN 4.17–18).

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Resembling parallels: DN 31 (PTS DN iii 180) Siṅgāla Sutta; AN 4.19 Tatiyaagatisutta; an4.17-18

**Sources**

- [Morris 1882] Richard Morris (ed.), Cariyāpiṭaka (1882) — Attested placement in the Dasanipāta and relationship to the Cariyāpiṭaka verses.
- [Bareau] André Bareau, Les récits canoniques du Cariyāpiṭaka et les Jātaka Pāli — Documented the Cariyāpiṭaka account of Cūlabodhi renouncing alongside his brāhmaṇī wife to fulfill the perfection of virtue.
- [Hazra 1994] Kanai Lal Hazra, Pali Language and Literature (1994) — Supplied narrative details regarding the king's abduction of Cūlabodhi's wife and the Bodhisatta's freedom from anger for sīlapāramī.
- [Anandajoti 2010] Bhikkhu Ānandajoti, Buddhist Wisdom Verses: 551 Verses from the Canon (2010) — Provided alternative title Cullabodhijātakam, narrative summary, and theme of destroying anger.
- [Brough] John Brough, The Chinese Pseudo-Translation of Ārya-Śūra's Jātaka-Mālā — Discussed Āryaśūra's Jātakamālā chapter 21 (Cuddabodhi) and its Tibetan translation corresponding to the Pali Jātaka.
- [War Yar Mein Da 2015] War Yar Mein Da, Paramis / Paramitas in Theravada and Mahayana (2015) — Noted the Bodhisatta's characterization as Cullaparibbājaka in Jātaka 443.
